goal: Interest score per chart and score order (S1, S2; Board gate 175: scoring only reorders, 8-chart cap selection unchanged, degenerate inputs score 0)
criteria: New app/score.py (stdlib only) with spearman (average ranks, by hand), pearson (statistics.correlation clamped to [-1, 1]), gini (x ascending, 2*sum(i*x_i)/(n*sum(x)) - (n+1)/n), skew (population g1); each returns a float in 0..1 (|rho|, |r|, Gini, min(1, |g1|/3)) and 0 for fewer than 2 values, constant values, negative category totals, sum 0 or any StatisticsError/ZeroDivisionError/OverflowError

Every rule in app/rules.py passes score=... to _chart from the full data before stride sampling: line = |Spearman| of per-time sums vs time, on that line's own value column; bar and donut = Gini of the category totals drawn; scatter = |Pearson r| of all pairs; histogram = skew of all values; heatmap = largest off-diagonal |z| (None skipped); map3d and country_map = 0.6, or 0 with fewer than 2 points/countries

rules.charts rounds each score with round(s, 2), cuts to MAX_CHARTS in rule order exactly as before, then sorts stably by -score (ties keep 3D map, country map, line, bar, donut, histogram, scatter, heatmap) and renumbers ids chart-1..N in display order

Every chart dict from GET /api/datasets/<id>/charts has a numeric 'score' in 0..1; on data_dir sales.csv the kinds are [line, histogram, bar, donut] with scores 0.89, 0.34, 0.23, 0.22; points.tsv map3d scores 0.6

Two identical requests return identical JSON; file 'k

Existing tests edited in this ticket: test_rules.py::test_sales_bar_and_line (kinds order, pick line and bar by kind, key set gains 'score'), test_rules.py::test_charts_route kinds, test_export_xlsx.py::test_sales_download (sheet list, chart_kinds order, histogram sheet name) and test_scatter_and_heatmap_from_numeric_file (re-run, do not guess), test_big_map_is_sampled and test_pages.py::test_big_csv_counts_have_separators (select the map3d by kind); any other test with a hard-coded chart order is re-run and fixed

goal: First load and filter speed levers (D1 part 1; Board gate 176: classify on the first 10,000 rows only, a 200,000-row CSV reaches the dashboard in <= 5 s cold)
criteria: profile.classify takes types from rows[:10000] only (deterministic; the 50%-of-total categorical rule uses the sample size); profile._kind counts each distinct string once with collections.Counter and calls _parses once per key (same result as before on every fixture)
rules heatmap computes pearson once per pair (j > i) and mirrors it; the z matrix equals the old one (test compares to a brute-force matrix on a small numeric file)

New rules.typed(columns, rows, mapping): copy of the rows with numerical and geospatial cells as _num(v) and temporal cells as _time(v); _num/_time return already-typed values unchanged; rules still work on raw rows (existing unit tests stay green)

app/main.py: @lru_cache(maxsize=4) _base(d) returns (rows, mapping, typed_rows) once per dataset; _charts and /api/datasets/<id>/profile use it; the page, charts API and both exports still give the same output as before this ticket; charts and KPIs use all loaded rows, only classification is sampled
tests/conftest.py make_client calls main._base.cache_clear() (and main._view.cache_clear() when it exists) so tests do not share caches

New tests/test_speed.py with big_sales_csv: cold GET /datasets/<id> (caches cleared, after the file is on disk) answers 200 in <= 5.0 s by time.perf_counter, and so does a cold GET charts API; a classify test with a column whose first 10,000 rows are numeric but a later row is text still returns numerical, and the sampled result equals the full result for every existing fixture; if the 5 s bound is missed, profile (cProfile in /tmp) and trim the next biggest cost before finishing
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_speed.py tests/test_profile.py tests/test_rules.py tests/test_pages.py passes

goal: Server-side filters, KPIs and the shared cached view (F1, K1, D1 part 2; Board gate 175: one value per column, filters AND, >50-distinct columns not categorical so no filter, KPIs follow the filters)
criteria: New app/filters.py: parse(params, columns, mapping) -> hashable tuple of (name, value) pairs: f.<column>=value for categorical columns only (empty value, unknown or non-categorical column ignored; repeated key keeps the last), then from, then to (valid date.fromisoformat on a dataset with a temporal column, else ignored, re-printed ISO); apply(f, columns, mapping, typed) -> kept row indexes or None when f == (); rows with an empty or unparseable time are dropped as soon as from or to is set; labels (e.g. 'region = North', 'date from 2024-01-01'); summary(labels) -> 'Filters: a; b' or 'Filters: none'; options(columns, rows, mapping) -> {categorical column: sorted distinct non-empty str values, <= 50}

_base also returns options; new @lru_cache(maxsize=8) _view(d, f) returns rows, mapping, options, filters, labels, charts (rules.charts on the filtered typed rows) and kpis; column types stay those of the unfiltered rows

New rules.kpis(columns, rows, typed, mapping) -> {'rows', 'columns', 'missing_pct' (round(100*empty/(rows*columns), 1), 0 when no cells; empty = None or ''), 'sums': [{'column', 'sum'}] for the first 3 numerical columns, int when whole else round(s, 2)}

GET /api/datasets/<id>/charts and the dashboard page call _view with filters.parse(request.query_params, ...); the charts API response gains 'kpis' and 'filters' (label list); with no params everything else answers as before; the page route passes view keys (kpis, options, labels, filters, a canonical query string) to the template without changing the template

sales.csv: ?f.region=North gives kpis.rows 3 and amount sum 16 and every chart total smaller than unfiltered; ?from=2024-01-03&to=2024-01-05 gives kpis.rows 3; unfiltered kpis Rows 6, Columns 3, missing_pct 0.0, amount sum 46; a column with more than 50 distinct values or an unknown f.column is ignored; a donut on the filtered column is simply not generated

On big_sales_csv, after one unfiltered warm-up request, GET charts?f.region=North answers 200 in < 1.0 s (time.perf_counter) with kpis.rows == 50000; tests in new tests/test_filters.py (unit tests of parse/apply/labels/summary/options plus the API checks)
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_filters.py tests/test_rules.py tests/test_pages.py tests/test_speed.py passes

goal: Filtered exports with XLSX Summary sheet and PPTX filter line (E1; Board gate 176: PPTX title slide shows 'Rows: N of M' when filtered, 'Rows: M' otherwise; gate 175: 'Filters: none' with no filters)
criteria: export.xlsx and export.pptx routes call _view(d, filters.parse(...)) like the charts API: the XLSX Data sheet holds the filtered raw rows and every chart the filtered data in score order

xlsx.write(dataset, rows, charts, summary='Filters: none') appends a last sheet named 'Summary' with A1 = summary; Data stays the first sheet and chart sheets keep their sheetN.xml positions; main passes filters.summary(view['labels'])

export.pptx(dataset, charts, summary='Filters: none', rows_shown=None) puts text 'Rows: M, C columns' on the title slide when unfiltered and 'Rows: N of M, C columns' when filtered (N filtered rows, M dataset rows, thousands separators), then a third text box with the summary line; direct calls without the new arguments still work

sales.csv ?f.region=North: XLSX Data has 3 data rows, first sheet 'Data', last sheet 'Summary' with A1 'Filters: region = North', the bar chart total is 16; no params gives A1 'Filters: none'; PPTX slide 1 contains 'Rows: 3 of 6' and 'Filters: region = North' filtered, 'Rows: 6' and 'Filters: none' unfiltered, and a chart's series values sum to the filtered total

Existing tests edited here: test_export_xlsx.py sheet lists end with 'Summary' (test_sales_download, the numeric-file test, the ['Data'] assertion becomes ['Data', 'Summary']); test_export_pptx.py slide-1 text assertions at lines 64, 99 and 137 change to the 'Rows: ...' form plus the 'Filters: none' box; exports of an unfiltered dataset still reopen in openpyxl and python-pptx
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_export_xlsx.py tests/test_export_pptx.py tests/test_filters.py passes

goal: Dashboard page: score caption, KPI strip, filter form, chips and filtered export links (P1; Board gate 175: removable chip per active filter plus Clear filters, 'table last' = First rows table stays below all charts, no score on it)
criteria: app/templates/dataset.html: after the page head a <dl class="kpis"> of <div><dt>/<dd> items Rows, Columns, Missing (as '0.0%'), '<column> (sum)' for up to three columns, every figure through the num filter, from the view's kpis (filtered rows when a filter is active)

A <form class="filters" method="get"> with one <div class="field"><label>…</label><select name="f.<column>"> per categorical column (empty first option, options from the view, the active value selected) and <input type="date" name="from">/<input type="date" name="to"> only when a temporal column exists, plus an Apply button; a dataset with no categorical or temporal column (notes.csv) shows no form

While a filter is active a <div class="chips-row"><ul class="chips"> shows one chip per filter with the label (e.g. 'region = North') and a remove link to the current URL without that filter (bare path when none is left), then a 'Clear filters' link to the bare dataset path; none of this is rendered with no filters

Each figure's .chart-rule text ends ' · score 0.NN' using the chart's score (2 decimals, same as the API); there is still exactly one .chart-rule and one .chart-count per figure; the Columns and First rows tables stay after the last , and Export PPTX/XLSX links carry the page's canonical filter query string

Markup matches docs/DESIGN.md Components so the existing databoot.css rules (.kpis, .filters, .field, .chips-row, .chips, first chart full width) apply; CSS is edited only if a measured problem is found at 1280 px and 390 px

goal: dashboard.js: filtered chart fetch, tidy form submit and click cross-filter with toggle (J1; Board gate 175: one value per column, clicking the active bar/slice again removes the filter)
criteria: dashboard.js fetches /api/datasets/<id>/charts with the page's location.search so the drawn charts equal the server-rendered filtered view; on submit the filter form drops empty fields from the URL (no 'f.region=' or empty from/to) so the address stays clean

A plotly_click on a bar chart or a donut slice whose column is categorical navigates (location.assign, so Back works) to the page URL with f.<column> set to the clicked category (x or label); if that column already has exactly that value the filter is removed instead; other filters stay (AND); other chart kinds do nothing

The clicked column name must reach the JS: if no existing chart field gives it (bar x_label, donut), add a data-column attribute to the figure in dataset.html (minimal change); charts of columns with more than 50 distinct values are not generated, so they never get a click filter
